transcript.content: Hi, I’m glad you came in. What brings you in today?

Yeah… thanks. I guess I’m here because I’ve been feeling like I’m kind of always running hot, if that makes sense. Like I can’t really shut the motor off.

I’ve managed okay for a long time, I think, but lately it’s been causing some issues at the firehouse, and I don’t want it to get worse or make things harder for the crew.
Have you ever had a period where you felt unusually high, euphoric, or full of energy compared with your normal self?

I don’t think so… I mean, I have times where I’m really keyed up or I’ve got a lot of energy, but that kind of feels like my usual baseline, if that makes sense.

I wouldn’t say I’ve had some stretch where I felt euphoric or like a totally different person. At least not that I’ve noticed. Does that answer what you’re asking?
Do you often have trouble staying focused on a task, even when you want to?

Yeah… I do. I mean, I try not to, and I don’t want it to sound like I’m not taking things seriously, because I am.

But in briefings, or even during drone training, I’ll be locked in for the first few minutes, and then I realize I’ve just been staring at the map or the screen and I didn’t catch half of what command just said. It’s frustrating, because I want to be focused. I’m not trying to drift off.
Looking back to when you were a kid, did you have this same kind of trouble staying focused?

Yeah… I think so. I mean, I don’t remember all of it perfectly, but my mom definitely says I was like this even back in grade school.

She’ll say I was always popping out of my seat, blurting out answers, losing homework… that kind of thing. I guess I got notes sent home a fair amount, even though I was bright enough to do the work. I don’t want to make it sound like I was a bad kid or anything—just… apparently it was there pretty early.
Do these focus problems cause trouble for you outside of work too?

Yeah… it does, though I try to keep on top of it.

It’s little everyday stuff that adds up. I’ll honestly mean to do something—like sign off on a training module, call someone back, pay a bill before there’s a late fee, or bring the right gear paperwork in for shift—and then it just slips. Not because I don’t care. I do care. I just… forget, and then I’m scrambling or apologizing.

I don’t know if that’s the kind of trouble you mean, but yeah, it’s not only at work.
Do you spend a lot of time worrying about everyday things, even when there isn’t a clear reason to?

I don’t think so… not a lot, anyway.

I mean, I worry about normal stuff—work, bills, making sure I didn’t forget something—but I wouldn’t say I’m sitting around worrying for no reason all the time. At least, I haven’t really noticed it like that. Is that what you mean?
Have you ever gone for several days needing much less sleep than usual and still felt rested?

No… I don’t think so.

I mean, with the firehouse schedule there are definitely times I don’t sleep much, but I don’t feel magically fine after it or anything. I’m usually tired like anyone would be. I can’t think of a time where I went several days on way less sleep and still felt rested.

final_diagnosis.reason: The interview supports attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder with persistent symptoms from childhood into adulthood across multiple settings. The patient confirms longstanding inattention (difficulty sustaining focus, drifting during briefings, forgetting tasks, losing track of responsibilities) and childhood hyperactive/impulsive behaviors (out of seat, blurting out answers, losing homework).
